Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public. 


Mazdoor  Kisan  Shakti  Sangathan 
"The  Right  to  Information,  The  Right  to  Live''

ISt«l33-1968 

Indian  Standard 

GENERAL  REQUIREMENTS  FOR 
HOSPITAL  FURNITURE 


0.    FOREWORD 

0.1  This  Indian  Standard  was  adopted  by  the  Indian  Standards  Institution 
on  24  April  1968,  after  the  draft  finalized  by  the  Hospital  Equipment 
Sectional  Committee  had  been  approved  by  the  Consumer  Products 
Division  Council. 

0.2  The  formulation  of  Indian  Standards  on  hospital  equipment  has  been 
taken  up  at  the  instance  of  the  Advisory  Committee  for  the  Development 
of  Surgical  Instruments,  Equipment  and  Appliances,  Government  of 
India. 

03  This  standard  forms  one  of  a  series  of  Indian  Standards  on  hospital 
furniture.    Other  specifications  in  the  series  are  as  foQows: 

IS :  4035-1 967  Trolleys,  stretcher 

IS :  403&- 1967  Trolleys,  patient 

IS :  4037-1967  Stretcher  and  stretcher  carriers 

IS :  4266-1967  Lockers,  bedside 

IS :  4267-1967  Stand,  wash  hand  basin 

IS :  4455-1967  Trolleys,  soUed  linen 

IS :  4458-1 967  Screens,  bedside 

IS :  4494-1968  Tables,  overbed 

0.4  This  standard  covers  such  requirements  as  are  general  and  common 
for  hospital  furniture.  Specific  requirements  for  different  items  of  hospital 
furniture  are  covered  in  relevant  specifications,  however,  in  case  of 
difference,  the  requirements  specified  in  the  particular  specification  shall 
apply. 

0.5  Thb  standard  contains  clauses  5  Jl  and  8.1  which  call  for  agreement 
between  the  purchaser  and  the  supplier  or  permit  the  purchaser  tp  exercise 
his  option  to  siut  his  requirement. 

0.6  For  the  purpose  of  dedding  whether  a  particular  requirement  of  this 
standard  is  complied  with,  the  final  value,  observed  or  calculated,  express- 
ing the  result  of  a  test  t>r  analysis,  shall  be  rcwnded  off  in  accordance  with 
IS :  2-1960*.  The  number  of  significant  places  retained  in  the  rounded  off 
value  should  be  the  same  as  that  of  the  specified  value  in  this  standard. 

*Rulei  foK  rounding  off  numerical  valuei  ( rmsitf ). 


18(4033-1968 

1.  SCOPE 

1.1  This  standard  coven  general  requirements  for  hospital  furniture. 

2.  MATERIAL 

2.0  The  materials  used  in  the  manufacture  of  hospital  furniture  shall  be  as 
specified  in  2.1  and  2.2. 

2.1  Frame  Work  —  Electric  resisunce  butt-weldcd  steel  tube  (  ERW ) 
conforming  to  IS :  2039-1964*. 

2.2  Top  —  This  shall  be  manufactured  from  any  of  the  following: 

a)  Mild  steel  sheet  either  coId-roUed  or  hot-roUed  quality. 

b)  Stainless  steel  sheet  conforming  to  Designation  04Crl9Ni9  or 
07Crl9Ni9  of  Schedule  V  of  IS :  1570^19611. 

c)  Aluminium  sheet  conforming  to  Grade  SIC  or  NS3  (|  H )   or 
NS4(JH)ofIS:737.1955t 

d)  Galvanized  steel  sheet  conforming  to  IS :  277-1962§. 

3.  SHAPES  AND  DIMENSIONS 

3.1  The  shapes  and  dimensions  of  hospital  furniture  shall  be  in  accordance 
with  the  requirements  of  relevant  specifications. 

4.  MANUFACTURE 

4.1  General  —  The  hospital  furniture  shall  be  properly  constructed  with 
all  welded  joints  sound,  clean  and  weU-formed.  Unless  otherwise  specified, 
the  vertical  mcfmbers  shall  be  perpendicular  to  the  wheel  base  and  parallel 
to  each  other  and  the  horizontal  members  shall  be  at  right  angles  to  the 
vertical  members.  Hospital  furniture  items  shall  stand  on  all  tiie  legs  at 
the  same  time  on  a  level  surface.  All  the  surfaces  shall  be  smooth  and  free 
from  pittings. 

4.2  Castora— The  castors  shall  be  held  securely  in  the  frame  by  any  of  the 
methods  of  attachment  specified  in  IS:  4034-1 968ll  and  shall  also  comply 
with  the  other  requirements  laid  therein.  The  castors  shall  turn  freely  in 
their  pivots  but  without  any  lateral  play.  The  wheels  shall  run  freely  in 
the  forks  and  shall  not  have  movement  in  anv  other  direction.  The  axle 
bolts  shall  pats  through  the  fork  ( horn )  and  oe  well  secured  by  huts. 

'Specification  for  ated  mbet  for  bicycle  and  allied  purpotet. 

tScbedulet  for  wroui^t  tted*  for  general  engineering  puipofci. 

tSpecificatiop  for  wrought  aluminium  and  aluminium  aOoya,  sheet  and  strip  ( for 
general  engineering  purposes •).(  Secomf  revasion  in  1974 }. 

ISpectficatioo  for  galvanised  sted  sheets  ( plain  and  corrugated  )  (fMMitf).(  Since  revised). 

llSpedfication  for  caston  for  hospital  e<|pi^Nnenc  * 


IS:4033-1968 

5.  FINISH 

5.1  All  mild  steel  parts  shall  be  painted  to  shades,  white,  ofF>white  or  sea 
green  ( No.  217  of  IS :  5-1961*  )  as  required  by  the  purchaser.  Prior  to 
painting,  all  the  parts  shall  be  degreased,  rust-proofed  by  phosphating  and 
then  suitably  protected  by  an  anti-corrosive  pruner,  either  by  brushing  or 
by  spraying  and  then  finished  by  spraying  in  stove  enamel  or  air-drying 
enamel  of  the  specified  shade.  In  every  instance,  each  coat 'shall  be 
separately  stoved  or  air  dried  as  the  case  may  be.  The  resulting  finish  shall 
be  hard  and  shall  not  readily  chip  or  flake. 

5.2  In  case  of  stainless  steel  or  aluminium.  It  shall  be  finished  bright  or 
satin  as  required  by  the  purchaser. 

5.3  Welding  shall  fully  penetrate  and  shall  be  sound  in  every  detail  and  it 
shall  be  finbhed  flush.  In  the  finished  stage,  there  shall  be  no  exposed 
sharp  edges  in  the  firame-work  or  other  unsealed  formations  which  may 
harbour  dirt  or  foreign  matter. 

6.  TESTS 

€.1  Hospital  furniture  items  shall  be  subjected  to  tests  in  accordance  with 
the  requirements  of  relevant  specifications.  However,  the  painted  furni- 
ture items  shall  also  satisfy  the  adhesion  test  described  in  6.1.1  and  if 
mounted  on  castors  these  shall  in  addition  satisfy  the  performance  test 
given  in  6.1.2. 

6.1.1  Adhesion  Test  —  A  square  measuring  (12* to  15  mm)  shall  be 
marked  over  conveniently  sdected  spot  on  the  painted  furniture  and  cross 
lines,  at  a  distance  of  1  to  1*5  mm  apart  and  inclined  at  120**,  shall  be 
inscribed  over  the  marked  portion  %vith  a  pointed  instrument.  Thereafter 
cdo-tape  shall  be  nibbed  do%m  over  this  portion  and  left  for  two  minutes; 
after  which  it  shall  be  jerked  free  from  the  painted  surface.  If  more  than 
5  percent  of  the  squares  had  ripped  away  from  the  painted  surface  and 
are  adhering  to  the  celo-tape,  the-  furniture  item  shall  be  repainted  and 
again  subjected  to  this  test  now  at  two  conveniently  selected  spots  and  the 
item  considered  passing  only  if  it  satisfies  in  both  the  cases. 

6.1.2  Performance  Test  —  When  the  item  is  pushed  over  a  level  and 
even  surface  with  or  Mrithout  load  ( load  to  be  as  laid  down  in  relevant 
specifications)  it  shall  not  wobble  or  rattle.  It  shall  also  move  freely 
when  pulled  in  circular  motion  and  the  castors  shall  face  in  the  same 
direction  without  much  effort. 

7.  MARKING 

7.1  Each  hospital  furniture  item  shall  have  a  nameplate  or  label  fixed  to  it 
showing  the  manufacturer's  name,  initiab  or  registered  trade-mark. 

♦Spedlication  Cor  oolouis  fbr  ready  nixed  painti  (  utmi  nmtim ). 

5 


IS»  4033- 1968 
7J.1  Each  item  may  also  be  marked  with  dhe  Standard  Mark. 

7.1.2  The  use  of  the  Standard  Mark  is  governed  by  the  provisions  of  Bureau  of 
Indian  Standar(te  Act,  1986  and  the  Rules  and  Regulations  made  thereunder. 
The  details  of  conditions  under  which  the  licence  for  the  use  of  Standard  Mark 
may  be  granted  to  manufacturers  or  producers  may  be  obtained  from  the  Bureau 
of  Indian  Standards. 

be  obtoioed  from  the  Bureau  of  Iiuli«ii  Siandards. 

8.  PACKING 

8.1  The  items  shall  be  packed  as  per  agreement  between  the  purchaser 
and  the  manufacturer.
